cli.description:
Subtitles (spoken language + target languages) for a YouTube video, a video file or all the videos
of a folder, from the command line.

    python -m subtitles <YouTube URL | video file | folder | .batch.json file> [options]

A folder becomes a batch, as in the web interface: a subtitles.batch.json file is written as the work goes, and
running the same command again after an interruption resumes where the batch stopped.

Web interface: python -m subtitles.web (see README). Settings come from config.toml overridden by
%LOCALAPPDATA%/subtitles/config.json (written by the web interface); the options below take precedence.
cli.idle: minutes without activity before stopping (default: [web] idle_min, 60; 0 = never)
cli.lang: language of the messages ({langs}); default: ui_language setting, else the system language
cli.list: show the configured engines and exit
cli.new_batch: batch: ignore the existing batch file and start again from the folder inventory
cli.no_subfolders: batch: only the videos of the folder itself
cli.open: open the page in the browser
cli.output: output folder (downloaded video, .srt; intermediate files in .travail/)
cli.port: listening port (default: [web] port of the configuration, 4420)
cli.redo: redo the transcription and the translation even if they exist
cli.source: YouTube URL, path of a video file, of a folder (batch) or of a .batch.json file
cli.spoken: spoken language (en, de…) if the detection is wrong
cli.targets: comma-separated target languages (fr,en…); default: target_languages setting
cli.transcription: id of a transcription server from the configuration
cli.translator: id of a translator from the configuration (local, claude, none…)
cli.until: batch: last step (default: traduction; doublage, assemblage into an MKV)
